V:
Sandhāna：A householder of Rājagaha．He was a follower of the Buddha，and it was his conversation with the Paribbājaka Nigrodha that led to the preaching of the Udumbarika Sīhanāda Sutta．

Buddhaghosa says （DA．iii．832） that he was the leader of five hundred upāsakas and was an anāgāmin．On one occasion，the Buddha sang his praises in the assembly for six qualities which he possessed．In the Anguttara he is mentioned in a list of eminent lay disciples （A．iii．451； cf．Dvy．540）．

Sandhiyate sandhi. Nirutti. 792. Dve padāni suṭṭhu dhiyatīti sandhi. Gaṭṭhunapyaṃ. 551. Dvinnaṃ padānaṃ antaraṃ adassetvā sammā dhīyatīti sandhi. Saddāpudacaca. Sandhi-saddo hi sarasandhi ādivācako pulliṅgo, paṭisandhiyādivācako itthiliṅgo sandhino sandhiyātiādidassanato. Nīti, pada. 334. Saṃdhi-saṃ, prā, addhamāgadhī. ] (1) (A) Edge or border (a place where two edges meet). Intervening space or time (or) Gap. Hole or perforation or puncture. (B) A joint (such as finger joint, ankle). (C) 180 Bone joints. A door leaves (which is for closing). (3) (A) It is connecting (such as it is connecting one word and another word). (Padasandhi, etc., it is 5 factors, one way- 6 factors). (B) It is combining letters and words, etc., (4) It is combining well two words cannot see their gaps Sandhi (Sarasandhi, etc.,). Sandhi Treatise (from grammatical Treatise). (6) (A) Fence (of one's yard). (B) House edge, Wall edge. (C) An edge of attachment house (Cyclic suffering house). (D) An edges (or) border that meet from one house's edges and another house's edges. Triangle junction road. A place of triangle junction road. (8) A place where meets two or more issues. (Uggaha) that meets (focusing Kammaṭṭhāna "Manasikāra") and (established or appeared Kammaṭṭhāna "Upaṭṭhāna"). (9) Rebirth-linking. (10) Makes an association. (It is love. Jataka. Vatthu). (3) Noble Truth. Vacīsacca. True words (sounds). (12) A cause (Five factors Sallekhapariyāya, etc.,). (13) The division or section. (14) Meaningless. "Padapuraṇa".

sandakasutta.p: [ sandaka + sutta ] (na) CL=7 Sandaka Sutta.
pn:
Sandakasutta. Ānanda, staying at the Ghositārāma in Kosambī, visits the Pilakkhaguhā near Devakaṭa pool, where the Paribbājaka Sandaka is staying with some five hundred followers. Ānanda is asked to give a discourse on the Buddha’s teachings, and speaks of the four antitheses to the higher life:

  • there is the teacher who holds that it does not matter whether actions are good or bad;

  • the teacher who holds that no evil is done by him who acts himself or causes others to act;

  • the teacher holding that there is no cause for either depravity or purity;

  • and, lastly, the teacher who holds, among other things, that men make an end of ill only when they have completed their course of transmigrations, like a ball of twine which continues rolling as long as there is string to unwind.

On these heresies cf. Sāleyyakasutta (MN 41). The reference is evidently to the teachings of Purāṇa Kassapa, Makkhali Gosāla and others.

Ānanda then proceeds to explain the four comfortless vocations: the teacher who claims to be all-knowing and all-seeing; the teacher whose doctrine is traditional and scriptural; the rationalist of pure reason and criticism teaching a doctrine of his own reasoning; and, lastly, the teacher who is stupid and deficient. Ānanda then describes the Buddha’s own teaching, leading up to the four Jhānas. Sandaka and his followers accept the Buddha as their teacher. MN.i.513-24.

pn:
Sandha. v.l. Saddha. A monk who visited the Buddha at Ñātikā in the Giñjakāvasatha, when the Buddha preached to him the Sandhasutta (q.v.). (AN.v.323f) (see GS.v.204, n.2; and 216, n.2).

It is, perhaps, the same monk who is mentioned as Saddho (v.l. Sandho) Kaccāyano (SN.ii.153, Giñjakāvasthasutta). He asks the Buddha a question on dhātu, and the Buddha explains it to him. In neither case does the Commentary say anything about Saddho (or Sandho).

The translator of the Saṁyutta regards saddho as an epithet.

sandhiccheda.p: [ sandhi + cheda=chidi + ṇa ] (ti) CL=7 One who has broken the connection (to a cycle of existence).

R:
sandhiccheda：သန္ဓိ-စေ္ဆဒ （ပ）
တိုက်စပ်ဖောက်ခြင်း။ ခြံစပ်ဖြတ်ခြင်း။ ပဋိစ္စသမုပ္ပါဒ်ကို ဖြတ်သော သူ။

sandhidvāra.p: [ sandhi + dvāra ] (na) CL=7 The mouth (opening) of a door of a house (or) it is a connected door.

sandhota.p: [ saṃ + dhū + ta.] (ti) CL=7 [Dhūdhātu kampanatthepi dhovanatthepi vattati. Nīti, dhātu. 251. In Pākatadhāna it is dhota=dhoa-puda dhāvadhātahu. Saṃdhovita-sakkatapikyapiṭaka.] It washed well.

sandhuni.p: [ saṃ + dhū + nā + ī ] (kri) CL=7 It has been abandoned.

sandhunāti.p: [ saṃ + dhū + nā + ti.] (kri) CL=7 [Nīti, dhātu. 249. Saṃdhunoti-saṃ.] (1) It makes face to the other side, push and shake it out. It makes face to that side. (bāḥ, Sya). It makes (beating, striking) from that side. (2) Abandon and remove it.

P: Sandhunāti，[saṁ+dhunāti] to shake D．II，336．（Page 678）
R:
sandhunāti：သန္ဓုနာတိ （သံ√ဓူ）
ကောင်းစွာ လှုပ်၏။ ထက်ဝန်းကျင်မှ လှုပ်၏။

sandhāgāra.p: [ saṃ + dhā + a= sandha + agāra.] (na) CL=7 [Santhamtana + agāra. Sandhi + agāra. Tacanaññaḥ- saha + agāra. Ha-kiu dha-pru. Niggahitalā. Sī, ṭī, saca, 1.65. See also - Santāgāra]. (1) Min Gun wayside public rest-house where is a gathering and meeting place. A Pavilion. (2) (Council of ministers in the time of Kings) where is a place of a legislature. (A) A Building that manages to go to the battlefront, and arrange the elephants, horses, Chariots, and soldiers. (B) When Kings go to war for two or three days and after coming back from the war, they rest in this building. (C) A place where a King and his counselors are gathering and meeting and a King orders his Counsellors for their country's benefit. (D) They gather and discuss social affairs in this building. (3) A place where makes sacrificial offerings and sacrificial rites are performed.

R:
sandhāgāra：သန္ဓာဂါရ （ပ）
မင်းတို့အမှုစီရင်ရာ မင်းကွန်း။ စည်ဝေးရာ အရပ်။သန္ထာဂါရ

sandhārayanta.p: [ saṃ + dhara + ṇaya + anta.] (ti) CL=7 [In Thī sandhārayantī.] It is supporting the firm.

sandhāretuṃ.p: [ saṃ + dhara + ṇe + tuṃ ] (bya) CL=7 (1) (a) To maintain or preserve. (bāḥ, Sya.). (B) To be strong (or) firm. To be steadfast. (2) To connect without a gap. (bāḥ, Sya.). To connect (or) relate. (3) To restrain. (To pardon).

sandhāvissaṃ.p: [ saṃ + dhātu + iṃ ] (kri) CL=7 [Iṃvibhatakiu issaṃ-pru. Nīti, sutta. 1103. Tacanaññaḥ- saṃ + dhāvu + ssaṃ] I will be wandering (going to and fro).

sandhāvitvāna.p: [ saṃ + dhāvu + tvāna ] (kri, vi) CL=7 See - Sandhāvitva.

sandituṃ.p: [ sanda + tuṃ.] (bya) CL=7 [From Sandati]. To flow (or) run.

sandiṭṭhi.p: [ saṃ + disa + ti.] (thī) CL=7 [Nirutti. 741. Saṃdapi-saṃ. ] (1) It is one's own belief. (2) Wisdom that should be praised. (3) One's opinion. (4) Opinion that appears in one's mind automatically.

P: Sandiṭṭhi，（f．） [fr．saṁ+dṛś] the visible world，worldly gain D．III，45，247； M．I，43； Sn．891； Vin．II，89； Nd1 288，300； °parāmāsin infected with worldliness M．I，97．（Page 677）
R:
sandiṭṭhi：သန္ဒိဋ္ဌိ （ဣ） （သံ√ဒိသ်+တိ）
ကောင်းစွာ မြင်ရခြင်း။

sandiṭṭhiparāmāsa.p: [ sandiṭṭhi + parāmāsa ] (ti) CL=7 (1) One who concentrates and contemplates his belief in the wrong way. (Pu) (2) Consideration for his belief in the wrong way.

R:
sandiṭṭhiparāmāsa：သန္ဒိဋ္ဌိ-ပရာမာသ （တိ）
မိမိအယူကို မှားသောအားဖြင့် သုံးသပ်သည်။

sandiṭṭhiparāmāsa：သန္ဒိဋ္ဌိ-ပရာမာသ （ပ）
မျက်မှောက်မြင်ဖူးသည်ကို သုံးသပ်ခြင်း။

sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī.p: [ sandiṭṭhiparāmāsa + ṇī.] (ti) CL=7 [In Thī -parāmāsinī.] One who concentrates and contemplates his belief in the wrong way.

R:
sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī：သန္ဒိဋ္ဌိ-ပရာမာသီ （တိ）
မိမိအယူကို မှားသောအားဖြင့် သုံးသပ်ခြင်း ရှိသည်။

sandiṭṭhirāga.p: [ sandiṭṭhi + rāga ] (pu) CL=7 (A) One who has Lust attached to his own wrong doctrine is his wealth. (B) Lust that happens together with one own wealth is a wrong doctrine. See also - Diṭṭhirāga. See also - Dīṭṭhirāga.

sandosa.p: [ saṃ + dosa.] (pu) CL=7 [Saṃdopa-sakkatapiṭaka.] One's flaws (or) defilements. See below.

P: Sandosa，[saṁ+dosa] pollution，defilement M．I，17； A．III，106，358； V，292； Sn．327．（Page 678）
R:
sandosa：သနေ္ဒာသ （ပ） （သံ√ဒုသ်+ဏ）
အပြစ်။

sandosahetu.p: [ sandosa + hetu ] (pu) CL=7 It is a cause of one's flaw (or) defilement.

sandālayitvā.p: [ saṃ + dala + ṇaya + tvā ] (kri, vi) CL=7 Having broken.

sandālayitvāna.p: [ saṃ + dala + ṇaya + tvāna ] (kri, vi) CL=7 See - Sandālayitva.

sandāpita.p: [ sanda + ṇāpe + ta ] (ti) CL=7 It was flowed (or) run.

sandīyati.p: [ saṃ + dā + ya + te ] (kamma, kri) CL=7 (1) It is troubled. (2) It is cut all.

R:
sandīyati：သန္ဒီယတိ （ကမ္မ） （သံ√ဒါ+ယ）
စိတ်မချမ်းသာ ဖြစ်၏။ နာကျည်း၏။သန္ဒိယျတိ

sandūseti.p: [ saṃ + dusa + ṇe + ti.] (kā, kri) CL=7 [Nirutti. 446-nhā. Saṃdūpayati-saṃ.] It destroys well.

saṇḍasaṇḍa.p: [ saṇḍa + saṇḍa ] (pu, na) CL=7 Clumped together.

saṇḍasaṇḍacārī.p: [ saṇḍasaṇḍa + cara + ṇī.] (ti) CL=7 [In Thī- -cārinī.] They gather and wander around.

P: Sandassana，showing J．I，67．（Page 677）
R:
sandassana：သန္ဒဿန （န） （သံ√ဒိသ်+ယု）
ကောင်းစွာ ပြခြင်း။ ဖူးမြင်ရခြင်း။ ထင်ခြင်း။

sandhisamalasaṅkaṭīra：သန္ဓိ-သမလ-သင်္ကဋီရ （န）
အိမ်ခြံစပ် မစင်ထုတ်သော ပြွန်။ တံမြက်ချေးစု။

sandhiyati：သန္ဓိယတိ （ကမ္မ） （သံ√ဓာ+ယ）
စပ်အပ်၏။ တပေါင်းတည်းဖြစ်၏။
sandhīyati：သန္ဓီယတိ
C: sandhīyati：[pass．of sandhāti] is connected，joined，or put together．
P: Sandhīyati，see sandahati．（Page 678）

R:
sandhāra：သန္ဓာရ （ပ）
ပျူငှာလောကဝတ်ပြုခြင်း။သန္ထာရ

sandhāvanikā：သန္ဓာဝနိကာ （ဣ）
လျင်စွာ ပြေးသွားခြင်း။
